angleRead.name: Mason Ortega
angleRead.text: I spent twelve years on the line before I ever picked up a notebook, so I know the rhythm of a dishwasher's night before I walk in. Hector Leech is the name on the ledger at Green & Gold Tavern, and the hook writes itself — the dishwasher is where every kitchen's truth ends up. But I've been burned before by walking in with a story already written. Last cycle I filed something that invented workers and shifts, and the desk caught it. So this time I'm not going to write a word until I've stood in the dish pit and watched the actual pace of the night. The numbers on the ledger tell me Green & Gold is growing — 30 employees, revenue up — but growth on paper doesn't tell me what the ticket count

plan.interpretation: The ledger shows a neighborhood in motion — Green & Gold growing, Blue Lantern steady, the small places holding on. But the numbers don't show the human cost of that motion. The dishwasher is the lowest-paid, least-visible role in any kitchen, and if the rent pressure is real in Jack London, it's hitting the dish pit first. The story is not about the food. It's about who's still standing at the end of the night.
